_comment: The hole register (#57). An export the corpus does not drive, recorded with a written reason. A hole is a
legitimate resting state and passes; an *undeclared* hole fails, which is the whole mechanism.
exports  the census entries this reason covers. A hole over an export something did drive fails as
stale, and so does one naming an export the census no longer carries — named per export, so a
reason that stopped being true of one of five says which one
reason   required. "The corpus has not reached it yet" and "nothing can ever drive it" are the same
absence, and telling those apart is the entire value of writing one down
ticket   optional, and written wherever an issue owns the closing. Its absence says nobody does yet
**One entry per reason, not per export** — the shape a region has, where one pattern claims many
differences. One entry per export would write the same sentence out thirteen times for the thirteen
exports it is true of, and a later edit would put the copies out of step with each other.
Failing on holes *themselves* was rejected: the net would be red from day one and stay red for months,
which trains people to ignore it. What fails is the residue — an export with neither a scenario nor an
entry here — and that is what the corpus's termination condition is stated against.
**This list is read by other work, not only by people.** Boundary stage 4 (#62) takes the components no
fixture mounts from it, and probed-variant selection (#59) takes the hooks and props exports nothing
drives — both derived from what is written here rather than hand-picked, which is why the reasons name
what would close them. `holesIn(outcomes, section)` in coverage/coverage.mjs is the query they call; it
joins this register to the census, so a consumer needs neither a section field here nor a reading of
the ticket links.
A hole does not stand in for a witness. Every export needs a rule in witnesses.json saying what driving it
would look like, the ones nothing drives included — otherwise nothing could ever report the hole closed.

holes.reason: no fixture portals anything. GraphView draws both containers for every flow whether or not the export is used, so a container in every trace says nothing — only content inside one does, which is what the witness asks for.

reachable only by an edge declaring the type, and the edges fixture declares none — every edge in the corpus renders as the default, which is BezierEdge. Each of their path functions has function parity, which is a different claim from the component rendering.
no fixture renders an edge toolbar. getEdgeToolbarTransform has function parity; the component is mounted by nothing, where its node-level sibling is driven by the node-toolbar fixture.

no fixture mounts a resizer. parity:boundary mounts both components with no props inside a node component, which is below the net and asserts no DOM; nothing in the corpus renders a resize control, and ticket 073 (XYResizer drag lifecycle) is what a scenario driving one would be measuring against.

no fixture passes an edgeTypes map, so no edge carries a type outside the built-in set. NodeTypes is driven because the node-toolbar fixture registers one; the edges fixture registers no edge type at all.

no fixture sets defaultEdgeOptions, and it has no DOM of its own — the options are merged into edges that declare none. Closing it needs a fixture whose edges declare no type and whose flow defaults them, which is the shape the witness names. No issue owns that fixture yet.

the rect exists only while the pointer is down, and every scenario that draws a selection box completes its gesture. `selection-box-mid-gesture` is the reserved scenario that ends with the pointer still down, which is the only way transient state is observed at all.

no scenario adds or replaces a node or an edge after mount. Every change the corpus records is a dimensions, position, select or remove; add and replace ride on the same handler, which is why the witness is the discriminant rather than the handler. `uncontrolled-update-node` and `flow-props-change-after-mount` are the reserved scenarios that would fire them.

the driver installs onReconnect and no scenario drags an edge endpoint onto another handle, so it never fires. The edgeupdater circles are in every edges-fixture trace, so the target exists and the gesture does not.
`shift-drag-selects-nodes` draws a selection and never drags the selection it made, which is the separate gesture these props fire on.

the driver withholds the prop (`parity/driver/callbacks.mjs`, HOLES), so no page installs it and no trace can record it. The reason recorded there — that onInit's ReactFlowInstance argument had not crossed the boundary — no longer holds: boundary stage 3 crosses `onInitIn` (`src/Boundary/Callbacks.purs`). Installing it and re-capturing the corpus is what closes this, and it is the first thing this artifact found that its own registers cannot fix.
a NodeResizer/NodeResizeControl prop rather than a ReactFlow one, so there is no handler for the driver to install and no fixture mounting either component. It needs a fixture that resizes.

the options record a hook is called with rather than a prop the flow is passed. The census files it under callbacks because what it carries is a callback, but nothing installs one — reaching it needs a probe component that calls the hook.

the hooks section is empty in every stored trace: it is keyed by probe id and no probe exists yet. A hook returns a value and leaves nothing on the page, so a component that renders nothing and reports what it was handed is the only thing that can observe one.

no scenario makes an imperative call. The `call` primitive exists and records into `api.calls`, so what is missing is a scenario and not a harness — `viewport-helpers-with-options` is the reserved scenario that drives the helpers with options.
the store's own shape, read through useStoreApi().getState() rather than through the instance the `call` primitive reaches. It needs the same probe the hooks section does.

the props section is empty in every stored trace, for the same reason the hooks section is: it is keyed by probe id and no probe exists. A node-level probe replaces a node type rather than wrapping it, which is what makes the props a component was handed observable at all.
